questions.question: Give three purposes of a business budget.
questions.expected_answer: Any three: plan income, expenses, stock and staff; control costs by comparing actual with budget; support decisions such as pricing; set targets; show lenders or partners that the business is well planned; ensure enough cash is available.

questions.question: A juice stall expects to sell 250 cups at R8. Fixed costs: stall hire R200. Variable costs: R3 per cup. Calculate budgeted income, total costs and expected profit.
questions.expected_answer: Income = 250 × R8 = R2 000. Variable costs = 250 × R3 = R750. Total costs = R200 + R750 = R950. Expected profit = R2 000 − R950 = R1 050.

questions.question: Explain favourable and unfavourable differences with one example of each.
questions.expected_answer: Favourable: actual results better for profit than budgeted (income higher or costs lower), e.g. sold 150 bags instead of 120. Unfavourable: worse for profit (income lower or costs higher), e.g. oil cost R5 per bag instead of R4; washing income R15 600 instead of R18 000.
